sentences.en: For many years, tech companies have been really good at innovation and making money.
sentences.zh: 多年来，科技公司在创新和赚钱方面一直非常出色。

sentences.en: What they've been less good at is in hiring and keeping a diverse workforce.
sentences.zh: 但他们在招聘和保持多元化员工队伍方面却表现欠佳。

sentences.en: In the past few months, frequent reports of Silicon Valley's rocky relationship with women have bubbled to the surface.
sentences.zh: 在过去几个月里，关于硅谷与女性关系紧张的报道屡见不鲜。

sentences.en: Very few women and non-Asian people of color in engineering.
sentences.zh: 工程领域的女性和非亚裔有色人种非常少。

sentences.en: Their diversity or lack of diversity and what they plan on doing to tackle it.
sentences.zh: 他们的多元化或缺乏多元化，以及他们计划如何解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Many companies have gone to great lengths to study the problem and to address it.
sentences.zh: 许多公司不遗余力地研究和解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Google, for example, spends tens of millions of dollars every year on efforts to recruit more women and people of color.
sentences.zh: 例如，谷歌每年花费数千万美元用于招聘更多女性和有色人种。

sentences.en: Some of that money went to produce this video.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分资金用于制作这段视频。

sentences.en: Make it really clear, we want to see more women in senior leadership positions.
sentences.zh: 明确一点，我们希望看到更多女性担任高级领导职务。

sentences.en: We want to see more people from underrepresented groups because it makes us a better company.
sentences.zh: 我们希望看到更多来自代表性不足群体的员工，因为这让我们成为一家更好的公司。

sentences.en: While there are recruitment success stories in Silicon Valley, the overall results have been dismal.
sentences.zh: 尽管硅谷有一些招聘成功的案例，但总体结果却令人沮丧。

sentences.en: Many women, African Americans and Latinos, say tech is unwelcoming to them.
sentences.zh: 许多女性、非裔美国人和拉丁裔人表示，科技界对他们并不友好。

sentences.en: Some have filed discrimination lawsuits against their companies.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至对他们的公司提起了歧视诉讼。

sentences.en: One senior software engineer at Google, James Damore, recently suggested his company and the tech industry were going about it all wrong.
sentences.zh: 谷歌的一位高级软件工程师詹姆斯·达莫尔最近指出，他的公司和整个科技行业的方法完全错了。

sentences.en: In an internal memo, he argued that the vast gender gap in technology wasn't the result of prejudice, but of biological differences between men and women.
sentences.zh: 在一份内部备忘录中，他认为科技界巨大的性别差距并非偏见所致，而是男女生物学上的差异造成的。

sentences.en: Damore cited research studies into the psychological and biological differences between the sexes.
sentences.zh: 达莫尔引用了关于两性心理和生物学差异的研究。

sentences.en: Women, he said, were more interested in people than things.
sentences.zh: 他说，女性对人比对物更感兴趣。

sentences.en: They had more anxieties and lower stress tolerance.
sentences.zh: 她们有更多的焦虑情绪，抗压能力较低。

sentences.en: They tended to be less confrontational.
This quality, he said, made it hard for them to ruffle feathers and take on leadership roles.
sentences.zh: 他说，这种特质使得她们很难掀起波澜并承担领导角色。

sentences.en: The memo created a firestorm inside the company.
sentences.zh: 这份备忘录在公司内部引发了一场轩然大波。

sentences.en: Many women at Google said it made them feel inferior and unwelcome.
sentences.zh: 谷歌的许多女性表示，这让她们感到自卑和不受欢迎。

sentences.en: When that memo was leaked to the world, Google was not happy.
sentences.zh: 当这份备忘录泄露给全世界时，谷歌非常愤怒。

sentences.en: Google has fired a software engineer who wrote a controversial internal memo that leaked over the weekend.
sentences.zh: 谷歌已经解雇了一名软件 engineer，因为他撰写了一份在周末泄露的充满争议的内部备忘录。

sentences.en: He claimed that biology, in part, explained why there were more men than women in the tech field.
sentences.zh: 他声称，生物学在一定程度上解释了为什么科技领域的男性多于女性。

sentences.en: Almost instantly, everyone seemed to have an opinion about the Google memo, the firing decision, and the larger question about women in tech.
sentences.zh: 几乎一瞬间，每个人似乎对谷歌备忘录、解雇决定以及关于科技界女性的更大问题都有了看法。

sentences.en: As far as I can see, they effectively have fired somebody for dissenting from the group consensus.
sentences.zh: 据我所见，他们实际上是因为某人不同意集体共识而解雇了他。

sentences.en: The crux of his argument was that women were inherently less competent to hold high-status positions, which is a biased opinion.
sentences.zh: 他论点的核心是女性天生不适合担任高地位职位，这是一种带有偏见的观点。

sentences.en: The infamous Google memo, the most important document since the Magna Carta...
sentences.zh: 臭名昭著的谷歌备忘录，自《大宪章》以来最重要的文件……

sentences.en: Damore said the media took his statements out of context.
sentences.zh: 达莫尔表示，媒体断章取义了他的言论。

sentences.en: His point, he said, wasn't to put down women or discourage them from entering tech.
sentences.zh: 他说，他的观点不是贬低女性或阻止她们进入科技行业。

sentences.en: It was to find solutions to the technology gender gap by acknowledging the differences between men and women and seeking ways to bridge them.
sentences.zh: 而是通过承认男女之间的差异并寻找弥合这些差异的方法，来找到解决科技领域性别差距的方案。

sentences.en: Science, he said, had conclusively found that nature trumps nurture, that women and men are different,
sentences.zh: 他说，科学已经得出结论，天性胜过培育，女性和男性是不同的，

sentences.en: and all the diversity training in the world couldn't change that.
sentences.zh: 世界上所有的多元化培训都无法改变这一点。

sentences.en: If you have an opinion about Damore, it probably comes in one of two flavors.
sentences.zh: 如果你对达莫尔有看法，那可能源于以下两种观点之一。

sentences.en: You might say, of course he's right.
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，他当然是对的。

sentences.en: Lots of scientists agree with him.
sentences.zh: 很多科学家都同意他的观点。

sentences.en: Political correctness is keeping us from acknowledging the obvious.
sentences.zh: 政治正确阻止了我们承认显而易见的事实。

sentences.en: Or you may say, this is just the latest effort to use science to advance a racist or sexist agenda.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能会说，这只是利用科学来推进种族主义或性别歧视议程的又一次尝试。

sentences.en: It's no different than people who used spurious science in the 19th century
sentences.zh: 这与19世纪人们利用虚假科学

sentences.en: to argue that blacks were slaves because they were inferior to whites.
sentences.zh: 来争辩黑人是奴隶，因为他们不如白人优越，没有任何区别。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we ask how much the gender differences we see in the world
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》中，我们探讨我们在世界上看到的性别差异

sentences.en: can be explained by genes and chromosomes
sentences.zh: 在多大程度上可以由基因和染色体解释

sentences.en: and how much they are the result of culture and the environment.
sentences.zh: 以及在多大程度上它们是文化和环境的结果。

sentences.en: Gender identity really is largely socially learned.
sentences.zh: 性别认同在很大程度上确实是社会习得的。
社会化无法凌驾于生物学之上。
这些分类甚至都不切实际。

sentences.en: And that was toxic to me because I could never, you know, fit into either one of those categories.
sentences.zh: 这对我有毒，因为我永远无法融入这两个类别中的任何一个。

sentences.en: You know, we're back to, I was never able to make peace with being a male.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们又回到了原点，我从来无法接受自己是个男性。

sentences.en: And I know that I'm not a female as well.
We're going to ask if this age-old debate really captures what we see in the world today.
sentences.zh: 我们要探讨这个陈旧的辩论是否真的抓住了我们今天在世界上看到的情况。

sentences.en: Is it possible the terms and categories of this debate are increasingly outdated?
sentences.zh: 这场辩论的术语和分类是否越来越过时了？

sentences.en: When the Google Memo hit the news, the talk shows went hunting for experts.
sentences.zh: 当谷歌备忘录成为新闻时，脱口秀节目开始四处寻找专家。

sentences.en: Let's go to our guest now.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们有请我们的嘉宾。

sentences.en: She is a writer about the intersection of science of sex and its politicization.
sentences.zh: 她是一位作家，研究性别科学的交集及其政治化。

sentences.en: in sexual neuroscience from York University.
And she has done quite a bit of work and research around this topic that we're going to get into with the Google Memo.
sentences.zh: 她围绕我们接下来要讨论的谷歌备忘录这个话题做了大量的工作和研究。

sentences.en: The one and only Dr. Deborah So is here.
sentences.zh: 独一无二的黛博拉·索博士来了。

sentences.en: Deborah So was in demand because, like former Google engineer James Damore, she is a firm believer that biology makes men and women different.
sentences.zh: 黛博拉·索之所以抢手，是因为和前谷歌工程师詹姆斯·达莫尔一样，她坚信生物学使男女有所不同。
黛博拉拥有神经科学博士学位

sentences.en: in neuroscience, but her opinions on gender are also personal.
sentences.zh: 但她对性别的看法也带有个人色彩。

sentences.en: When we got in touch, she told me that when she was young, she did not feel much like a girl.
sentences.zh: 当我们联系时，她告诉我，她小时候并不觉得自己像个女孩。
我所有的朋友都是男孩。
黛博拉说她觉得自己是男性。

sentences.en: She has helped conduct studies into the nature of gender.
sentences.zh: 她曾协助开展关于性别本质的研究。

sentences.en: She thinks both her outlook and her interest in science stem from her biology.
sentences.zh: 她认为自己的世界观和对科学的兴趣都源于她的生物学特性。

sentences.en: I do think that I personally was exposed to higher levels of testosterone in the womb.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为我个人在子宫里接触到了更高水平的睾酮。

sentences.en: That's Deborah's simple explanation for her boyness.
sentences.zh: 这是黛博拉对她具有男孩气概的简单解释。

sentences.en: The levels of exposure to prenatal testosterone is actually the determining factor in terms of what children will be interested in,
sentences.zh: 接触产前睾酮的水平实际上是决定儿童会对此感兴趣的因素，

sentences.en: what they will gravitate towards in terms of their interests and behaviors.
sentences.zh: 他们在兴趣和行为方面会倾向于什么。

sentences.en: In some ways, Deborah's point of view sounds pretty old-fashioned.
sentences.zh: 从某些方面来看，黛博拉的观点听起来相当老派。

sentences.en: Boys tend to gravitate towards mechanically interesting things, so they tend to be interested in things.
sentences.zh: 男孩往往倾向于机械性有趣的事物，所以他们往往对物品感兴趣。

sentences.en: When they're playing with toys, they'll gravitate towards trucks and cars.
sentences.zh: 当他们玩玩具时，他们会倾向于卡车和汽车。

sentences.en: Girls tend to be more interested in socially interesting activities, so things like playing with dolls and playing house.
sentences.zh: 女孩往往对社交上有趣的活动更感兴趣，比如玩洋娃娃和过家家。

sentences.en: But Deborah says the science backs her up with many studies.
sentences.zh: 但黛博拉说，科学通过许多研究支持了她的观点。

sentences.en: She gives one example of a research study on girls who have a genetic condition called congenital adrenal hyperplasia.
sentences.zh: 她举了一个关于患有先天性肾上腺皮质增生症的女孩的研究例子。

sentences.en: These girls are exposed to unusually high levels of testosterone in the womb,
sentences.zh: 这些女孩在子宫里接触到异常高水平的睾酮，

sentences.en: and what we see when they are born is they will gravitate towards male-typical toys.
sentences.zh: 我们看到她们出生时，会倾向于男性化的玩具。

sentences.en: And this is even if their parents give them more praise for playing with female-typical toys.
sentences.zh: 即使她们的父母因为她们玩女性化玩具而给予更多表扬，也是如此。

sentences.en: So it speaks to how powerful biology is, and that gender identity and gender preferences can't really be molded as much by socialization.
sentences.zh: 这说明了生物学有多么强大，性别认同和性别偏好实际上无法被社会化塑造太多。

sentences.en: Testosterone masculinizes the brain, Deborah says.
sentences.zh: 黛博拉说，睾酮使大脑男性化。

sentences.en: You can see this play out in many ways.
sentences.zh: 你可以在很多方面看到这种表现。

sentences.en: Men's brains, on average, are bigger than women's,
sentences.zh: 平均而言，男性的脑容量比女性大，

sentences.en: and there are differences in the connective tissue in the brain's white matter.
sentences.zh: 大脑白质中的结缔组织也存在差异。

sentences.en: There are more connections running from the front to the back of the brain in men,
sentences.zh: 男性大脑从前往后的连接更多，

sentences.en: and more connections running left to right or interhemispherically in women.
sentences.zh: 而女性大脑从左到右或半球间的连接更多。

sentences.en: So this leads to in adulthood differences.
sentences.zh: 这导致了成年后的差异。

sentences.en: I mean, this is evident from a very young age as well in terms of what children gravitate naturally towards,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从很小的年纪起，儿童自然倾向于什么，这也显而易见，

sentences.en: differences in terms of efficiency of processing.
sentences.zh: 在处理效率方面也存在差异。

sentences.en: So men tend to be more efficient, on average, when it comes to visual-spatial processing,
sentences.zh: 因此，在视觉空间处理方面，男性平均效率更高，

sentences.en: whereas women tend to be more efficient with processing analytically and intuitively.
sentences.zh: 而女性在分析和直觉处理方面效率更高。

sentences.en: In animals, researchers have observed behavioral changes after birth
sentences.zh: 在动物研究中，研究人员观察到，如果在子宫内改变睾酮水平，

sentences.en: if testosterone levels are changed in utero.
sentences.zh: 出生后的行为会发生变化。

sentences.en: In the wild, male and female monkeys behave differently.
sentences.zh: 在野外，雌雄猴子的行为有所不同。

sentences.en: Monkeys are not socialized to prefer certain toys over others,
sentences.zh: 猴子并没有被社会化要求偏好某些玩具胜过其他玩具，

sentences.en: and we see the same thing with male monkeys.
sentences.zh: 我们在雄性猴子身上看到了同样的情况。

sentences.en: They tend to gravitate towards trucks and cars,
sentences.zh: 它们往往倾向于卡车和汽车，

sentences.en: wheeled toys that boys tend to find more interesting.
sentences.zh: 男孩往往觉得更有趣的有轮玩具。

sentences.en: And we see the same thing with female monkeys.
sentences.zh: 我们在雌性猴子身上也看到了同样的情况。

sentences.en: They tend to gravitate towards more socially interesting toys like dolls.
sentences.zh: 它们往往倾向于更有社交趣味的玩具，比如洋娃娃。

sentences.en: The bottom line, says Debra, is that men and women are different.
sentences.zh: 黛博拉说，归根结底，男女是不同的。

sentences.en: These differences are so obvious that she gets frustrated when people argue that gender is a social construct.
sentences.zh: 这些差异如此明显，以至于当人们争辩说性别是一种社会建构时，她会感到沮丧。

sentences.en: To Debra, that doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 对黛博拉来说，这说不通。

sentences.en: If we look at it from an evolutionary perspective,
sentences.zh: 如果我们从进化的角度来看，

sentences.en: we will, and I think people who take the socialization approach will agree,
sentences.zh: 我们会，而且我认为采取社会化方法的也会同意，

sentences.en: when we look at men and women on average,
sentences.zh: 当我们平均看待男女时，

sentences.en: men tend to be taller than women.

sentences.zh: 我们的生殖器官是不同的。

sentences.en: So they'll acknowledge and accept that there are these differences
sentences.zh: 所以他们会承认并接受这些差异

sentences.en: in terms of biology and physiology,
sentences.zh: 在生物学和生理学方面，

sentences.en: but for some reason, those differences stop at the brain.
sentences.zh: 但出于某种原因，这些差异在大脑这里就停止了。

sentences.en: And I don't think that makes much sense,
because when you look at the brain as an organ,
sentences.zh: 因为当你把大脑看作一个器官时，

sentences.en: it's responsible for these differences that we see with regards to organs and growth.
sentences.zh: 它负责我们在器官和生长方面看到的这些差异。

sentences.en: Believing that biology shapes the choices men and women make
sentences.zh: 相信生物学塑造了男女的选择
并不意味着她是性别歧视者，

sentences.en: nor is she advocating lesser roles for women.
sentences.zh: 她也不是在倡导降低女性的角色。

sentences.en: In her view, these two things have nothing to do with each other.
sentences.zh: 在她看来，这两者毫无关系。

sentences.en: The scientific findings should be allowed to stand on their own.
sentences.zh: 科学发现应该允许其自行成立。

sentences.en: You know, if we acknowledge that men and women are different,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我们承认男女不同，

sentences.en: because this is what biology is telling us,
sentences.zh: 因为这就是生物学告诉我们的，

sentences.en: that doesn't mean that they shouldn't be equal.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着他们不应该平等。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that one is necessarily better than the other.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着一方一定比另一方更好。

sentences.en: And I think also there's this sense that female typical traits
sentences.zh: 而且我认为人们也有一种感觉，即女性典型特质

sentences.en: are somehow inferior to male typical traits.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上不如男性典型特质。

sentences.en: And I think that's the thing that we should be talking about.
sentences.zh: 我认为这才是我们应该讨论的事情。

sentences.en: Not, you know, pretending that women and men are absolutely identical
sentences.zh: 而不是假装女性和男性完全相同，

sentences.en: and that the only differences we see are due to socialization.
sentences.zh: 并且我们看到的唯一差异是由社会化引起的。

sentences.en: In a sense, this is exactly the point that former Google software engineer
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这正是前谷歌软件工程师
詹姆斯·达莫尔所要表达的观点。

sentences.en: If you accept that men and women are biologically programmed to have different interests,
sentences.zh: 如果你承认男女在生物学上注定有不同的兴趣，

sentences.en: then all the efforts to get more women to become engineers can look foolish.
sentences.zh: 那么所有试图让更多女性成为工程师的努力看起来就会很愚蠢。

sentences.en: But there's a problem with this view.
sentences.zh: 但这种观点存在一个问题。

sentences.en: When we look at the world, we have a tendency to think that the way the world is,
sentences.zh: 当我们看待世界时，我们有一种倾向，认为世界的现状

sentences.en: is the way the world is supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 就是世界本该有的样子。

sentences.en: Women are supposed to be kind and affectionate.
sentences.zh: 人们总认为女性应该温柔体贴。

sentences.en: Men are supposed to be tough and dominant.
sentences.zh: 人们总认为男性应该坚强强势。

sentences.en: Similar arguments to the ones that James and Deborah are making
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯和黛博拉提出的类似观点

sentences.en: were made a couple of generations ago to explain why Caucasians were smarter than Asians.
sentences.zh: 在几代人之前就被用来解释为什么高加索人比亚洲人更聪明。

sentences.en: There were very few Asians in American scientific institutions
sentences.zh: 当时美国的科学机构中极少有亚洲人

sentences.en: and very few Asian Nobel Prize winners,
sentences.zh: 获得诺贝尔奖的亚洲人也寥寥无几，

sentences.en: so it seemed reasonable to say that there was something about the biology of Asians
sentences.zh: 因此人们似乎顺理成章地认为亚洲人的生物学特性

sentences.en: that made them bad at science and tech.
sentences.zh: 让他们不擅长科学和技术。

sentences.en: Today, we'd find that idea laughable.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们会觉得这种想法荒谬可笑。

sentences.en: Again, because we see so many examples of Asians excelling at places like Google.
sentences.zh: 同样，因为我们看到太多亚洲人在谷歌这样的地方大放异彩的例子。
如果生物学决定了现实，

sentences.en: how can that reality change dramatically in just a few decades?
sentences.zh: 这种现实怎么会在短短几十年内发生如此巨大的变化？

sentences.en: In a moment, we'll take a deeper look at the brain
sentences.zh: 稍后，我们将深入探讨大脑

sentences.en: and what neuroscience can tell us about gender choices.
sentences.zh: 以及神经科学能为我们揭示怎样的性别选择。

sentences.en: But first, I want you to meet an historian.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我想向大家介绍一位历史学家。

sentences.en: She thinks many of the choices that men and women and boys and girls make today
sentences.zh: 她认为当今男人、女人、男孩和女孩做出的许多选择

sentences.en: are shaped by norms, by culture, even by marketing.
sentences.zh: 都是由社会规范、文化甚至市场营销塑造的。

sentences.en: I met Joe Paoletti at a mall in suburban Maryland.
sentences.zh: 我在马里兰州郊区的一个购物中心采访了乔·保莱蒂。

sentences.en: I'm a professor in American Studies at the University of Maryland.
sentences.zh: 我是马里兰大学美国研究专业的教授。

sentences.en: Joe is also the author of the book, Pink and Blue,
sentences.zh: 乔也是《粉红与蓝色》一书的作者，

sentences.en: which explores the history of how we dress our children.
sentences.zh: 该书探讨了我们如何为孩子穿衣的历史。

sentences.en: So I always head right for the infant's department first
sentences.zh: 所以我总是直奔婴儿服装区

sentences.en: to see how much pink there is
and how many things you could put either a boy or a girl in.
sentences.zh: 以及有多少款式是男孩女孩都可以穿的。

sentences.en: The children's clothing section at Macy's is packed with racks of onesies,
sentences.zh: 梅西百货的童装区摆满了挂着连体衣的衣架，

sentences.en: dresses, and tiny suits for the under-7 set.
sentences.zh: 还有针对7岁以下儿童的裙子和小西装。

sentences.en: It is, Joe told me, an excellent place for a history lesson.
sentences.zh: 乔告诉我，这里是上历史课的绝佳场所。

sentences.en: You know, one of my taglines that I'm going to put on my business card
sentences.zh: 你知道，我打算印在名片上的座右铭之一

sentences.en: is, I think, deep thoughts about shallow things.
sentences.zh: 我想大概是，用深刻的思想研究肤浅的事物。

sentences.en: It's what you do when you study popular culture.
sentences.zh: 当你研究流行文化时，你就会这么做。

sentences.en: You can't just say, oh, I'm only going to study the intellectual stuff.
sentences.zh: 你不能只说，哦，我只研究那些高深的东西。

sentences.zh: 自20世纪80年代中期以来，乔一直通过

sentences.en: by strolling through the clothing section of mainstream retailers.
sentences.zh: 逛主流零售商的服装区来关注性别规范。

sentences.en: In recent years, she's noticed more gender-neutral options for kids.
sentences.zh: 近年来，她注意到儿童有了更多中性服装的选择。

sentences.en: But mainly, she says, children's clothing remains predictable.
sentences.zh: 但她说，主要来说，童装依然没有什么新意。

sentences.en: Boys mostly wear the same palette of colors.
sentences.zh: 男孩穿的颜色大体上还是那几种。

sentences.en: A lot of navy blue and olive and brown and black and gray.
sentences.zh: 大量海军蓝、橄榄绿、棕色、黑色和灰色。

sentences.en: The boys' shirts, sweaters, jackets, and pants
sentences.zh: 男孩的衬衫、毛衣、夹克和裤子

sentences.en: have pictures of trucks, bulldozers, sports cars, and cute macho sayings.
sentences.zh: 上面印着卡车、推土机、跑车和可爱的男子气概标语。
就连婴儿的衣服也是如此。

sentences.en: Joe points to a stack of onesies.
There's dude, and we have a puppy,
and we have an alien coming out of a pocket.
sentences.zh: 还有从口袋里钻出来的外星人。

sentences.en: Matter of fact, the two out of the first four have little pockets,
sentences.zh: 事实上，前四件里有两件都有小口袋，

sentences.en: even though they're not functional anymore.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们已经没有任何实际功能了。

sentences.en: It's a pocket because he's a boy.
sentences.zh: 之所以有口袋，是因为他是个男孩。

sentences.en: Little brother, super rad like dad,
Next, we head over to the girls' section.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们前往女孩服装区。

sentences.en: It's overflowing with soft and cheerful hues.
sentences.zh: 这里到处都是柔和欢快的色调。

sentences.en: It used to be the pastels were kind of summer colors,
sentences.zh: 过去，柔和的浅色调有点像夏季的颜色，

sentences.en: and now pastels are girl colors all year round.
sentences.zh: 而现在，浅色调成了全年女孩专属的颜色。

sentences.en: But if I'm looking at sort of things like this, for example,
sentences.zh: 但如果我看着诸如此类的东西，比如，

sentences.en: in the racks over here, it feels like there's absolutely no question
sentences.zh: 在前面的这些衣架上，感觉毫无疑问

sentences.en: We have not only a flamingo, but a flamingo with flowers on it
sentences.zh: 我们不仅有火烈鸟，还有身上带着花朵

sentences.en: and a bow on its head, so you know it's a girl flamingo.
sentences.zh: 头上还戴着蝴蝶结的火烈鸟，这样你就知道这是一只母火烈鸟了。

sentences.en: Why do so many of us dress little boys and little girls so differently?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们大多数人把小男孩和小女孩打扮得如此不同？

sentences.en: A hundred-odd years ago, Joe says,
small kids were all dressed the same, in frocks.
sentences.zh: 小孩子们穿的都一样，都是长袍。

sentences.en: And partly what it was was people really thought that drawing a child's attention
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，人们真的认为引导孩子注意

sentences.en: to what their sex was was bad.
sentences.zh: 他们的性别是一件坏事。

sentences.en: That to the late 19th century mind, early 20th century,
sentences.zh: 在19世纪末和20世纪初的人看来，

sentences.en: the cause of any kind of sexual depravity was precocious sexuality.
sentences.zh: 任何形式的性堕落的根源都在于早熟的性意识。

sentences.en: Like a little girl should not be thinking in terms of being a woman someday,
sentences.zh: 就像小女孩不应该想着有朝一日成为女人一样，

sentences.en: a little boy must not be thinking that he's like daddy
sentences.zh: 小男孩也不能觉得自己像爸爸，

sentences.en: until it's kind of developmentally appropriate.
sentences.zh: 直到这在发育上是恰当的年龄。

sentences.en: And back at that time, that developmental appropriateness
sentences.zh: 而在那个时期，这种发育上的恰当性

sentences.en: So by the time they were four or five,
sentences.zh: 所以到他们四五岁的时候，

sentences.en: a lot of the advice comes when the mothers are writing in and saying,
sentences.zh: 许多咨询信件都是母亲们写来的，她们会问：

sentences.en: when should I put my little boy in trousers?
sentences.zh: 我什么时候该给我家小男孩穿裤子？

sentences.en: Because they'd be wearing little dresses.
sentences.zh: 因为他们一直穿着小裙子。

sentences.en: And he's tall for his age, or he's this, or he's that.
sentences.zh: 而且他个子长得高，或者他这样，或者他那样。

sentences.en: And he'd say, well, you wait till he insists upon it.
sentences.zh: 然后人们会说，嗯，等到他自己坚持要穿再说。

sentences.en: So it was the idea that your gender was innate,
sentences.zh: 所以当时的观点是，你的性别是天生的，

sentences.en: and you would start to express it later.
sentences.zh: 你会在晚些时候开始表现出来。

sentences.en: But if you put children in, put a little, put a baby in pants,
sentences.zh: 但如果你让孩子们穿上，给一个，给婴儿穿上裤子，

sentences.en: they would be, well, they'd be horrified at the little girls in pants
sentences.zh: 他们会，嗯，他们会对穿裤子的女孩

sentences.en: and the little boys in pants, because pants were just not for babies.
sentences.zh: 和穿裤子的男孩感到震惊，因为裤子根本不是给婴儿穿的。

sentences.en: In the 1950s, many boys and girls wore similar navy and maroon outfits to school.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代，许多男孩和女孩穿着相似的海军蓝和栗色服装去上学。
游戏时穿的衣服也是深色的。

sentences.en: Pastels were thought appropriate only for holidays like Easter or formal occasions.
sentences.zh: 人们认为浅色只适合复活节等节日或正式场合。

sentences.en: But gradually, the distinction between boys' clothes and girls' clothes started to grow.
sentences.zh: 但渐渐地，男孩服装和女孩服装的区别开始扩大。

sentences.en: By the 1970s, American families were having fewer kids.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪70年代，美国家庭的孩子生得越来越少。

sentences.en: Fewer kids meant families needed fewer clothes.
sentences.zh: 孩子变少意味着家庭需要的衣服也变少。

sentences.en: For retailers, fewer clothes sold meant fewer dollars.
sentences.zh: 对零售商而言，卖出的衣服变少意味着赚到的钱变少。

sentences.en: So they came up with an ingenious way to sell more stuff.
sentences.zh: 于是他们想出了一个巧妙的办法来卖出更多东西。

sentences.en: They marketed the idea that clothes defined what it was to be a boy or a girl.
sentences.zh: 他们推销这样一种观念：服装决定了什么是男孩或女孩。

sentences.en: The more you make something individual, the more you can sell.
sentences.zh: 你把某种东西个性化的程度越高，你能卖出的就越多。

sentences.en: So having something that can only be worn by a girl
sentences.zh: 因此，如果某种东西只能由女孩穿着，

sentences.en: means it can less likely be handed down to a brother.
sentences.zh: 这就意味着它很难再传给弟弟穿。

sentences.en: This led to a small bit of marketing genius.
sentences.zh: 这带来了一个堪称营销天才的小创意。

sentences.en: What we think of now as it's just a law, right, that pink is for girls and blue is for boys.
sentences.zh: 我们现在觉得这就像一条铁律，对吧，粉色属于女孩，蓝色属于男孩。

sentences.en: If you made pink a girl's color and blue a boy's color, then male and female siblings couldn't wear the same clothes.
sentences.zh: 如果你把粉色变成女孩的颜色，蓝色变成男孩的颜色，那么兄弟姐妹就不能穿同一件衣服了。

sentences.en: Marketing wasn't the only force at work.
sentences.zh: 市场营销并不是唯一的驱动力。

sentences.en: Societal biases came into play that allowed girls to sometimes wear blue, but made it hard for boys to ever wear pink.
sentences.zh: 社会偏见也发挥了作用，它允许女孩偶尔穿蓝色，却让男孩几乎很难穿粉色。

sentences.en: I look around and I see plenty of blue things and nobody says, oh, she's wearing blue.
sentences.zh: 我环顾四周，看到到处都是蓝色物品，没有人会说，哦，她穿着蓝色。

sentences.en: She must be a boy or she's wearing blue.
sentences.zh: 她一定是个男孩，或者她穿着蓝色。

sentences.en: Her mother must be making a statement about gender politics.
sentences.zh: 她母亲一定是在对性别政治表态。

sentences.en: But if a boy wears pink, there always has to be some kind of explanation.
sentences.zh: 但如果一个男孩穿粉色，总得做出某种解释。

sentences.en: Because it goes back to the idea from the early unisex period in the 60s and 70s that it is better to be a boy than a girl.
sentences.zh: 因为这可以追溯到60和70年代无性别时期的观点，即当男孩比当女孩更好。

sentences.en: That for a girl to want to be like a boy, that's understandable.
sentences.zh: 如果一个女孩想变成男孩子的样子，那是可以理解的。

sentences.en: And she'll grow out of it.
sentences.zh: 她长大后就会自然改变。

sentences.en: But for a boy to want to be like a girl, that's deviant and he must be taken to therapy.
sentences.zh: 但如果一个男孩想变成女孩子的样子，那就是越轨行为，必须送去接受心理治疗。

sentences.en: Or at least expect to be made the butt of jokes, like in this episode of Friends.
sentences.zh: 或者至少要做好成为笑柄的心理准备，就像《老友记》里的这一集一样。
有人看到我的衬衫了吗？

sentences.en: It's buttoned down like a faded salmon color.
sentences.zh: 是那种扣起来的褪色三文鱼色衬衫。

sentences.en: No, I haven't seen your pink shirt.
sentences.zh: 不，我没看到你的粉色衬衫。

sentences.en: I must have left it at Mona's.
sentences.zh: 我一定把它落在莫娜家了。

sentences.en: I'm sure you can get another one of Dan Taylor's.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定你能从丹·泰勒那儿再弄一件。

sentences.en: But seriously, what's interesting about Joe's point is it shows that what today might seem like individual gender choices
sentences.zh: 但说真的，乔的观点有趣的地方在于它表明，今天看起来像是个人的性别选择

sentences.en: are actually driven by many hidden factors.
sentences.zh: 实际上是由许多隐藏的因素驱动的。
金钱、营销、恐同、性别歧视。

sentences.en: Does this mean that biology has no role in shaping what boys and girls and men and women do?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着生物学在塑造男孩、女孩、男人和女人的行为方面毫无作用？

sentences.en: It turns out the contention that genes and prenatal testosterone don't matter
sentences.zh: 事实证明，认为基因和产前睾酮无关的观点

sentences.en: is as simplistic as saying they explain everything.
sentences.zh: 和认为它们能解释一切的观点一样过于简单化。

sentences.en: Nature and nurture are completely intertwined.
sentences.zh: 先天与后天是完全交织在一起的。

sentences.en: And there is no such thing as nature without nurture and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 没有离开后天的先天，反之亦然。

sentences.en: We're exploring today the differences between the sexes and the debate over where such differences come from.
sentences.zh: 我们今天在探讨两性之间的差异，以及这些差异究竟源自何处的争论。

sentences.en: One thing that's not up for debate?
sentences.zh: 有一件事是毫无争议的吗？

sentences.en: An important part of how we understand people is to ask if someone is male or female.
sentences.zh: 我们理解他人时的一个重要部分，就是询问某人是男是女。

sentences.en: This is why, when a baby is born, everyone wants to know.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，当婴儿出生时，每个人都急于知道。

sentences.en: Gender is unquestionably the most salient feature of a person's identity.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，性别是个人身份中最显著的特征。

sentences.en: That's the first thing we notice about someone,
sentences.zh: 这是我们对一个人注意到的第一件事，

sentences.en: and it's certainly the first characteristic that infants learn to discriminate.
sentences.zh: 也绝对是婴儿学会分辨的第一个特征。

sentences.en: She's a professor of neuroscience at Rosslyn Franklin University in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 她是芝加哥罗莎琳·富兰克林大学的神经科学教授。

sentences.en: For some two decades, she's pondered and researched differences between boys and girls.
sentences.zh: 近二十年来，她一直在思考和研究男孩与女孩之间的差异。

sentences.en: Lise says she first became interested in the subject as she was writing a book on brain development,
sentences.zh: 莉斯说，她最初对这个主题产生兴趣是在撰写一本关于大脑发育的书时，

sentences.en: but she became immersed in the topic after her own children were born.
sentences.zh: 但在她自己的孩子出生后，她真正全身心投入到了这个话题中。

sentences.en: We had a daughter and a couple of sons, and as many parents will tell you, they seem so different.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个女儿和几个儿子，正如许多父母会告诉你的那样，他们看起来如此不同。

sentences.en: And that certainly is one of the favorite conversations among parents is gender differences.
sentences.zh: 这当然也是父母们最喜欢讨论的话题之一，那就是性别差异。

sentences.en: So I set out to do the research and really educate myself and translate to others what's truly known about the differences between boys' and girls' brains.
sentences.zh: 所以我着手进行研究，真正充实自己，并向其他人阐明关于男孩和女孩大脑差异的真正科学认知。

sentences.en: Lise didn't start by looking at boys' brains and girls' brains.
sentences.zh: 莉斯并不是从研究男孩和女孩的大脑开始的。

sentences.en: She started with an insight about all brains.
sentences.zh: 她是从对所有大脑的一个深刻见解开始的。

sentences.en: More than any other organ, the brain is uniquely adaptable, designed to change in response to the environment.
sentences.zh: 与其他任何器官相比，大脑具有独特的适应性，专为随环境变化而改变而设计。

sentences.en: My own research has always been in the area of neuroplasticity, or how our brains change as a result of experience.
sentences.zh: 我自己的研究一直集中在神经可塑性领域，也就是我们的大脑如何因经验而改变。

sentences.en: And so I'm always sort of acutely aware of the fact that these little babies are absorbing things from the moment of birth.
sentences.zh: 因此，我总是敏锐地意识到一个事实：这些小婴儿从出生的那一刻起就在吸收各种事物。

sentences.en: If you think of the brain not as a computer that comes with a chip and a hard drive,
sentences.zh: 如果你把大脑看作不是那种自带芯片和硬盘的计算机，

sentences.en: but more like a liquid designed to take the shape of the vessel that it's in, you start to get the idea.
sentences.zh: 而是更像一种旨在适应其所处容器形状的液体，你就会开始明白这个道理了。

sentences.en: When a baby is born, its brain comes programmed not with the ability to learn one specific language,
sentences.zh: 当婴儿出生时，其大脑的编程并不是为了学习某一种特定的语言，
而是为了学习任何语言。

sentences.en: The infant brain is designed to learn from everything that's going on around it.
sentences.zh: 婴儿的大脑旨在从其周围发生的一切中进行学习。

sentences.en: Much of that starts by being alert to the social world.
sentences.zh: 其中很大一部分始于对社交世界的敏锐感知。

sentences.en: It's remarkable the degree of understanding babies have way before they can talk,
sentences.zh: 婴儿在还不会说话之前，

sentences.en: way before they can even reach out and grab a rattle under control.
sentences.zh: 甚至在还不会伸手有意识地抓摇铃之前，就表现出惊人的理解力。

sentences.en: They appreciate the motives of other people.
sentences.zh: 他们能理解其他人的动机。

sentences.en: They can tell the difference between a good guy and a bad guy.
sentences.zh: 他们能够分清好人和坏人。

sentences.en: And as I said, they can also discriminate gender, and they start learning quite early
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，他们也能分辨性别，并且很早就开始学习

sentences.en: the distinction between male and female, how their mother and father behave differently.
sentences.zh: 男性和女性的区别，以及他们的父亲和母亲行为上的不同。

sentences.en: So it's built in from the very get-go of social and communicative development.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是从社交和沟通能力发展的最初阶段就内置的东西。

sentences.en: Although babies are unaware of their own gender, within the first few months of life,
sentences.zh: 尽管婴儿在生命的前几个月里并不了解自己的性别，

sentences.en: they can tell the difference between male and female voices and male and female faces.
sentences.zh: 但他们能分辨出男性和女性的声音以及男性和女性的面孔。

sentences.en: They are absorbing clues to gender identity.
sentences.zh: 他们正在吸收关于性别认同的线索。

sentences.en: Once children figure out they're a boy or girl, which happens somewhere in the third year of life,
sentences.zh: 一旦孩子们弄明白自己是男孩还是女孩（这通常发生在生命第三年的某个时候，

sentences.en: when they really have a solid understanding, it becomes a great crystallizer for their own behavioral decisions.
sentences.zh: 当他们有了确切的理解时），这就会成为他们自身行为决策的巨大催化剂。

sentences.en: Lise doesn't dismiss the power of biology, but she thinks many of us fail to see what neuroscientists know.
sentences.zh: 莉斯并没有忽视生物学的作用，但她认为我们中的许多人未能看到神经科学家所了解的事实。

sentences.en: The brain not only is shaped, but has to be shaped by the social world.
sentences.zh: 大脑不仅被社交世界塑造，而且必须由社交世界来塑造。

sentences.en: When we see differences between men and women, and then see differences in their brains,
sentences.zh: 当我们看到男人和女人之间的差异，然后又看到他们大脑中的差异时，

sentences.en: we intuitively think, voila, this must explain why Johnny likes trucks and Jane likes dolls.
sentences.zh: 我们直觉地会认为，瞧，这一定能解释为什么约翰尼喜欢卡车而简喜欢洋娃娃。

sentences.en: But Lise believes the human brain is basically intersex, or non-gendered, with one major exception.
sentences.zh: 但莉斯认为，人类的大脑基本上是双性同体的，或者说是无性别的，只有一个重大例外。

sentences.en: Since men tend to be physically larger than women,
sentences.zh: 由于男性的体型通常比女性大，

sentences.en: the male brain is also likely to be larger than the female brain.
sentences.zh: 男性的大脑也往往比女性的大脑要大。

sentences.en: You know, my view is, of course, there are group-level differences between men and women,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的观点是，男人和女人之间当然存在群体层面的差异，

sentences.en: but they're statistical, and they are not categorical.
sentences.zh: 但它们是统计学意义上的，而不是绝对类别的。

sentences.en: So, whereas our reproductive organs come in two types,
sentences.zh: 因此，虽然我们的生殖器官分为两种类型，

sentences.en: they come in testes or ovaries, and some other parts as well,
sentences.zh: 即睾丸或卵巢，以及其他一些部位，

sentences.en: our brains come in one type, and it's a spectrum from masculinity to femininity.
sentences.zh: 但我们的大脑只有一种类型，它是一个从男性化到女性化的光谱。

sentences.en: The male brain and female brain are no more different than the male heart and the female heart,
sentences.zh: 男性大脑和女性大脑的差异并不比男性心脏和女性心脏的差异大，

sentences.en: than the male kidney and the female kidney,
sentences.zh: 也不比男性肾脏和女性肾脏的差异大，

sentences.en: which, by the way, also are all proportionally larger in men than women.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这些器官在男性身上也按比例比女性更大。

sentences.en: Now, there used to be a time when scientists thought that the size of the brain was really important.
sentences.zh: 以前曾有一段时间，科学家认为大脑的大小极其重要。

sentences.en: Phrenologists measured the size and shapes of people's skulls,
sentences.zh: 颅相学家测量人们头骨的大小和形状，

sentences.en: and then drew sweeping conclusions about people from different groups.
sentences.zh: 然后对不同群体的人得出宏大的结论。

sentences.en: But more recent work has challenged the idea that bigger always means different.
sentences.zh: 但最近的研究对“更大总是意味着不同”这一观点提出了质疑。

sentences.en: I've done several studies looking at structures that are alleged to differ between men and women.
sentences.zh: 我做过几项研究，考察据称在男女之间存在差异的脑部结构。

sentences.en: One is the hippocampus, which is important for memory,
sentences.zh: 一个是海马体，这对记忆很重要；

sentences.en: and the other is the amygdala, which is important for emotion and fear.
sentences.zh: 另一个是杏仁核，这对情绪和恐惧很重要。

sentences.en: And both of these structures have been alleged to differ between adult men and women,
sentences.zh: 这两个结构都被认为在成年男女之间存在差异，

sentences.en: but when we did a meta-analysis, basically downloading all of the dozens and dozens of studies
sentences.zh: 但当我们进行元分析——基本上是下载了所有数十项

sentences.en: of comparing men and women's brains,
sentences.zh: 比较男女大脑的研究时，

sentences.en: it turns out there is no difference between the hippocampus of men and women
sentences.zh: 结果发现，一旦针对整体大脑尺寸进行校正，

sentences.en: or the amygdala of men and women once you correct for overall brain size.
sentences.zh: 男女的海马体或杏仁核之间其实并没有差异。

sentences.en: Lise agrees with Deborah Soh, the scientist we heard from earlier,
sentences.zh: 莉斯赞同我们之前听过其采访的科学家黛博拉·索（Deborah Soh）的观点，

sentences.en: who believes that hormone levels in utero can affect the brain of the baby.
sentences.zh: 后者认为子宫内的激素水平会影响婴儿的大脑。

sentences.en: But where Deborah sees hormonal influence as decisive, Lise thinks of it as just a nudge.
sentences.zh: 但黛博拉将激素的影响视作决定性的，莉斯则认为它只是一种推波助澜的作用。

sentences.en: There are probably some properties of toys that may appeal more to boys and girls,
sentences.zh: 玩具可能确实有一些属性，会“本能地”
对男孩和女孩更有吸引力。

sentences.en: There's so much more layered on top of that in terms of the marketing,
in terms of the parent and grandparent encouragement,
sentences.zh: 在父母和祖父母的鼓励方面，

sentences.en: in terms of especially peer reinforcement,
sentences.zh: 特别是在同龄人的强化方面，还有太多的后天叠加因素，

sentences.en: because we see that there's almost no gender difference before the first birthday
sentences.zh: 因为我们发现，在儿童周岁生日之前，

sentences.en: in the type of toys that children prefer.
sentences.zh: 他们在偏好的玩具类型上几乎没有性别差异。

sentences.en: There's a little hint of it, maybe at about nine months.
sentences.zh: 也许在九个月左右时有一点点迹象。

sentences.en: But it's really once children start to gender identify,
sentences.zh: 但真正到了孩子们开始认同性别时，

sentences.en: and especially once they start breaking up into separate playgroups,
sentences.zh: 特别是当他们开始分成不同的游戏群体时，

sentences.en: because gender segregation happens beginning about age three,
sentences.zh: 因为性别隔离大约从三岁开始，

sentences.en: that the differences in preference become extremely pronounced.
sentences.zh: 偏好的差异就会变得极其明显。

sentences.en: So there's a, I would say, a strong social role,
sentences.zh: 所以我想说，社会角色的影响很强，

sentences.en: a modest, innate or instinctive role.
sentences.zh: 而天生或本能的角色的影响则比较温和。

sentences.en: And you put those two together,
sentences.zh: 当你把这两者结合起来，

sentences.en: and you end up with a very dramatic divergence by the time kids are four years old.
sentences.zh: 到孩子们四岁时，你就会发现他们走向了截然不同的分化方向。

sentences.en: A host of scientific studies have found evidence
sentences.zh: 大量科学研究发现了证据，

sentences.en: of the powerful role that social influences play.
sentences.zh: 证明社会影响发挥了强大的作用。

sentences.en: There was this recent study out of Emory University
sentences.zh: 埃默里大学最近开展了一项研究，

sentences.en: and they had these nice audio recorders,
sentences.zh: 他们佩戴了精良的音频记录器，

sentences.en: so the parents weren't aware of every moment, every interaction.
sentences.zh: 因此父母并不知道每一个时刻、每一次互动的细节。

sentences.en: And it turned out that the fathers were commenting
sentences.zh: 结果发现，父亲们更多地评论

sentences.en: more on their daughter's physical appearance,

sentences.zh: 更多地评论她们的肚子，

sentences.en: and also endorsing their daughter's feelings more than their son's,
sentences.zh: 而且比对儿子那样更支持女儿的情感，

sentences.en: basically reacting more to their son's neutral expressions
sentences.zh: 基本上是对儿子的中性表情反应更多，

sentences.en: and more to their daughter's sad or fearful expressions.
sentences.zh: 而对女儿的悲伤或恐惧表情反应更多。

sentences.en: And so we do this because we have different expectations for males and females,
sentences.zh: 我们之所以这样做，是因为我们对男女有着不同的期望，

sentences.en: and that has to do with our very deep-seated gender assumptions.
sentences.zh: 这与我们根深蒂固的性别假设有关。

sentences.en: Lise also cites a study with mothers and their 11-month-old babies.
sentences.zh: 莉斯还引用了一项针对母亲及其11个月大婴儿的研究。

sentences.en: The infants are put on a, what looks like a crazy steep slope to crawl down,
sentences.zh: 婴儿被放在一个看起来极其陡峭的斜坡上让他们往下爬，

sentences.en: but it's carpeted and it has a gating up on the sides so it's safe.
sentences.zh: 但斜坡铺了地毯，两侧有护栏，所以很安全。

sentences.en: And it turns out when mothers were asked to adjust the steepness of the slope
sentences.zh: 结果发现，当要求母亲们调整斜坡的陡度，

sentences.en: for the steepest slope they thought their babies were capable of crawling down,
sentences.zh: 调到她们认为自己婴儿有能力往下爬的最陡坡度时，

sentences.en: the mothers turned it to a steeper slope for their sons than their daughters,
sentences.zh: 母亲们为儿子设置的坡度比女儿的更陡，

sentences.en: and then when the infants were actually tested,
sentences.zh: 然而当对婴儿进行实际测试时，

sentences.en: there was actually no difference in the courageousness
sentences.zh: 男婴和女婴在敢于尝试的勇气

sentences.en: or the physical ability of baby boys and girls to crawl down a steep slope.
sentences.zh: 或沿陡坡往下爬的身体能力上其实并没有区别。

sentences.en: In yet another study, both mothers and fathers discouraged risk-taking on the playground
sentences.zh: 在另一项研究中，母亲和父亲对女儿在游乐场上的冒险行为的阻止，

sentences.en: for their daughters more than for their sons.
So when you start doing that when kids are 1 and 2 and 3 years old,
sentences.zh: 因此，当你从孩子们1岁、2岁和3岁时就开始这样做，

sentences.en: it really sets them on different trajectories.
sentences.zh: 这确实让他们走上了不同的发展轨迹。

sentences.en: Without necessarily intending to treat sons and daughters differently,
sentences.zh: 成年人在未必有意区别对待儿子和女儿的情况下，

sentences.en: adults also subtly communicate expectations about language, math, and spatial skills.
sentences.zh: 也会潜移默化地传达出关于语言、数学和空间技能的期望。
例如，来自以色列的研究

sentences.en: found that sixth-grade teachers in Tel Aviv schools
sentences.zh: 发现特拉维夫学校的六年级老师

sentences.en: give girls slightly lower math scores than they deserve
sentences.zh: 给女孩的数学评分略低于她们应得的分数，

sentences.en: and give boys slightly higher math scores than they deserve.
sentences.zh: 而给男孩的数学评分略高于他们应得的分数。

sentences.en: By high school, the children often end up with different beliefs
sentences.zh: 到了高中，孩子们往往会对

sentences.en: about their own ability in math.
sentences.zh: 自己数学能力产生不同的信念。

sentences.en: Males and females are both capable of learning spatial skills and verbal skills perfectly well.
sentences.zh: 男女完全都有能力学习好空间技能和语言技能。

sentences.en: It really is largely a matter of dose of experience that determines our differences.
sentences.zh: 我们的差异很大程度上确实是由经验的“剂量”决定的。

sentences.en: Here's what all these studies together tell us.
sentences.zh: 所有这些研究共同向我们说明了这一点。

sentences.en: Social norms that treat girls and boys in different ways are all around us,
sentences.zh: 以不同方式对待男女的社会规范在我们周围无处不在，

sentences.en: and even the most diligent parents will find that they can control
sentences.zh: 甚至最尽职的父母也会发现，他们只能控制

sentences.en: only a small fraction of the influences shaping their children.
sentences.zh: 塑造孩子影响中的一小部分。

sentences.en: You cannot erase gender from a child's experience.
sentences.zh: 你无法从孩子的经历中抹去性别。

sentences.en: There's no such thing as a gender-free society.
sentences.zh: 根本不存在什么无性别社会这一说。

sentences.en: And parents who claim that they're raising children gender-neutral,
sentences.zh: 那些声称自己正在以无性别方式抚养孩子的父母——

sentences.en: we treated our son and daughter exactly the same, are really fooling themselves.
sentences.zh: “我们对待儿子和女儿完全一样”——其实是在自欺欺人。

sentences.en: Lee says that doesn't mean people should stop trying to push back against gender stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 莉斯表示，这并不意味着人们应该停止尝试打破性别刻板印象。

sentences.en: What we can do is we can say what kind of society do we want to have
sentences.zh: 我们能做的是，我们可以明确我们想要拥有一个什么样的社会，

sentences.en: and what are the experiences that young children are immersed in
sentences.zh: 以及幼儿们沉浸在什么样的经历中，

sentences.en: that will either make boys and girls have more similarity of opportunity
sentences.zh: 这些经历是会赋予男孩和女孩更多的机会相似性，

sentences.en: or will drive a wedge between them.
sentences.zh: 还是会在他们之间制造隔阂。

sentences.en: And I think in our society we're always striving for greater equality,
sentences.zh: 我认为在我们的社会中，我们一直在争取更大的平等，

sentences.en: and so we need to think about how to maximize the brain potential of both genders
sentences.zh: 因此我们需要思考如何最大化两种性别的脑力潜力，

sentences.en: as opposed to slot them into these limited roles
sentences.zh: 而不是将他们塞进这些有限的角色中，

sentences.en: that really don't allow them to express the full range of humanity.
sentences.zh: 因为这些角色实在无法让他们充分表达人性。

sentences.en: As I talked to scientists Lise Elliott and Deborah So
sentences.zh: 在与科学家莉斯·埃利奥特（Lise Eliot）和黛博拉·索（Deborah Soh），

sentences.en: and to historian Joe Paoletti, I realized that all of them agreed on one thing.
sentences.zh: 以及历史学家乔·保莱蒂（Joe Paoletti）交谈时，我意识到他们在一件事上达成了一致。

sentences.en: People ought to be allowed to live their lives,
sentences.zh: 人们应该被允许过他们自己的生活，

sentences.en: to be all they want to be,
regardless of what the world tells them they should be.
sentences.zh: 而不管世界告诉他们应该成为什么样的人。

sentences.en: Toward the end of his memo on gender issues,
sentences.zh: 在关于性别问题的备忘录接近尾声时，
谷歌工程师詹姆斯·达莫尔（James Damore）表示，

sentences.en: I hope it's clear that I'm not saying that diversity is bad,
sentences.zh: 我希望大家清楚，我并不是说多样性不好，

sentences.en: that we shouldn't try to correct for existing biases,
sentences.zh: 我们不应该努力纠正现有的偏见，

sentences.en: or that minorities have the same experience of those in the majority.
sentences.zh: 或者少数群体与多数群体的经历是一样的。

sentences.en: I'm also not saying that we should restrict people to certain gender roles.
sentences.zh: 我也没有说我们应该把人们限制在某些特定的性别角色中。

sentences.en: I'm advocating for quite the opposite.
Treat people as individuals, not as just another member of their group.
sentences.zh: 把人当作个体来对待，而不是仅仅当作他们所属群体的另一个成员。

sentences.en: The person we're going to hear from next has never talked to James Damore or Deborah So,
sentences.zh: 我们接下来要采访的人从未与詹姆斯·达莫尔或黛博拉·索交谈过，

sentences.en: never taken a class with Joe Paoletti or Lise Elliott.
sentences.zh: 也从未上过乔·保莱蒂或莉斯·埃利奥特的课。

sentences.en: But I'm sure I know what this person, Jamie Shoup,
sentences.zh: 但我确信我知道这个人——杰米·舒普（Jamie Shoup）——

sentences.en: would say to the idea that we should treat people as individuals
sentences.zh: 会对“我们应该把人当作个体来对待，

sentences.en: and not as just another member of their group.
sentences.zh: 而不是仅仅当作他们所属群体的另一个成员”这一观点说些什么。

sentences.en: The reason I went to court to blow all of this up was,
sentences.zh: 我之所以诉诸法庭来打破这一切，是因为

sentences.en: and I think we're a mixture to some extent of male and female,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们在某种程度上是男性和女性的结合体，

sentences.en: When we come back, what Jamie Shoup,
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，杰米·舒普（Jamie Shoup），

sentences.en: the first legally recognized non-binary person in the United States,
sentences.zh: 美国第一位在法律上获得承认的非二元性别者，

sentences.en: can tell us about the great gender debate.
sentences.zh: 将为我们讲述关于这场伟大性别之争的看法。
这里是“隐藏的大脑”（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: We've been talking today about gender
sentences.zh: 我们今天一直在讨论性别

sentences.en: and about our long-running debates over the role of biology versus culture.
sentences.zh: 以及我们长期以来关于生物学与文化作用的争论。

sentences.en: For many years, these debates have largely assumed that gender is a binary,
sentences.zh: 多年来，这些争论在很大程度上假设性别是二元的，

sentences.en: But even as science struggles to understand the male brain and the female brain,
sentences.zh: 但正当科学努力理解男性大脑和女性大脑时，

sentences.en: some people are challenging the reality of those fundamental categories.
sentences.zh: 一些人正在挑战这些基本类别的现实性。

sentences.en: Jamie Shoup is in the vanguard of that movement.
sentences.zh: 杰米·舒普正是这场运动的先锋。

sentences.en: Jamie just pulled into Carson City, Nevada,
sentences.zh: 杰米刚刚把车开进内华达州的卡森城，

sentences.en: after roaming around the West for the past few months
sentences.zh: 过去几个月里，他一直在美国西部四处游荡，

sentences.en: in a small camper perched on top of a pickup truck.
sentences.zh: 开着一辆小房车，车身就架在一辆皮卡货箱的顶部。

sentences.en: So basically we're in what's called a truck camper.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上我们住的是所谓的皮卡房车。

sentences.en: In other words, heavy and small, but also efficient.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，又重又小，但也高效。

sentences.en: I've got a microwave, an oven, a stove, you know, double sink,
sentences.zh: 我有一个微波炉、一个烤箱、一个炉灶，你知道的，双槽洗手池，

sentences.en: a small bathroom with a shower.
sentences.zh: 还有一个带淋浴的小浴室。

sentences.en: Jamie's at ease in this desert town,
sentences.zh: 杰米在这个沙漠小镇里显得很自在，

sentences.en: clad in jeans, a flowing blouse, and headscarf.
sentences.zh: 穿着牛仔裤、飘逸的衬衫和头巾。

sentences.en: The camper has been traveling a lot of late,
sentences.zh: 这辆房车最近一直在四处奔波，

sentences.en: but for now, Jamie's biggest journey is over,
sentences.zh: 但对目前来说，杰米最漫长的旅程已经结束了，

sentences.en: a rocky trip over the landscape of gender identity.
sentences.zh: 那是一段在性别认同风景中充满坎坷的旅程。

sentences.en: I think the best way to frame this and understand it
sentences.zh: 我认为界定和理解这一点的最好方式

sentences.en: is to just think of me as very fluid.
sentences.zh: 就是把我视为非常流动的人。

sentences.en: Jamie thinks not of himself or of herself,
sentences.zh: 杰米不把自己视为他或她，

sentences.en: I can be masculine, I can be feminine,
sentences.zh: 我可以是男性的，我也可以是女性的，

sentences.en: I can do anything I want.
sentences.zh: 我可以做任何我想做的事。

sentences.en: Jamie is the first officially recognized,
sentences.zh: 杰米是美国第一位官方承认的、

sentences.en: It was a status that had to be fought for and won.
sentences.zh: 这是一个必须通过抗争才能争取并赢得的身份。

sentences.en: It came after a five-decade struggle,
sentences.zh: 这经历长达五十年的挣扎，

sentences.en: a struggle to find an identity that felt right.
sentences.zh: 一场寻找一个感觉正确的身份的挣扎。

sentences.en: Now 54 years old, Jamie was born in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 现年54岁的杰米出生在华盛顿特区，

sentences.en: and raised in a large blue-collar family in rural southern Maryland.
sentences.zh: 在马里兰州乡村南部的一个大型蓝领家庭中长大。

sentences.en: It was a place of tobacco farms and deep conservative views.
sentences.zh: 那是一个满是烟草农场和浓厚保守观念的地方。

sentences.en: This is a place where the black kids that I cut tobacco with during the summer,
sentences.zh: 这是一个我在夏天一起割烟草的黑人孩子，

sentences.en: they weren't allowed in the farmers' houses because they were black.
sentences.zh: 因为他们是黑人而不能进入农场主家里的小镇。

sentences.en: I mean, it was that kind of place.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就是那种地方。

sentences.en: There were no gay people, there were no trans people.
sentences.zh: 那里没有同性恋者，也没有跨性别者。

sentences.en: You know, football consisted of being called Smear the Queer.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，橄榄球游戏就是被人叫作“消灭同性恋（Smear the Queer）”。

sentences.en: Jamie was different and didn't fit in with the boys.
sentences.zh: 杰米与众不同，无法融入男孩们的圈子。

sentences.en: As a teenager, I was reading fashion magazines
sentences.zh: 作为一个青少年，我在读时尚杂志

sentences.en: and doing things like, you know, putting,
sentences.zh: 并且做一些事情，比如，你知道，把……

sentences.en: I remember one occasion I read an article
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次我读了一篇文章

sentences.en: about putting mayonnaise and egg in your hair to make it soft,
sentences.zh: 关于把蛋黄酱和鸡蛋抹在头发上能让头发变软，

sentences.en: and my mother absolutely just went ballistic over that
sentences.zh: 我妈妈对此简直气炸了，

sentences.en: and slapped me and called me a sissy.
sentences.zh: 狠狠地扇了我一巴掌，还骂我是娘娘腔。
杰米的母亲也彻底崩溃了，

sentences.en: when the teenager refused to get a short haircut
sentences.zh: 当这个少年拒绝剪短发
